A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SE-LLM research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison; the missing stability table in v8 is a content removal rather than an extraction gap.

before.justification: v6 reports original long-term, short-term, and zero-shot forecasting results, component and backbone ablations, efficiency measurements, and three-seed stability results.

after.justification: v8 retains original forecasting results, ablations, qualitative analysis, and efficiency measurements, although it removes the separate statistical-stability results.

M1.justification: Two operations within TSCC are revised: Equation 3 and Algorithm 2 switch from semantic queries with temporal keys/values to temporal queries with semantic keys/values; Equation 4 and Algorithm 4 replace standardized correlation with segment-averaged, L2-normalized similarity. The surrounding architecture remains. The sequential Time-Adapter wording clarifies the sequence already shown and described in v6.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ETT, Weather, Traffic, ECL, Solar, M3, and M4 coverage, including the same forecasting and frequency-transfer scenarios. Removing repeated-seed results and one M4 comparator does not remove dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: TimeMixer++ is removed from the M4 short-term comparisons in Tables 2 and 10, including its average SMAPE/MASE/OWA results of 11.884/1.597/0.856. It remains in the long-term comparisons. Other comparator memberships are retained.

E3.justification: The retained splits, forecasting horizons, model configurations, and evaluation procedures match. Both versions already describe baseline runs across different input lengths. Correcting QWA to OWA in Section 4.1 does not introduce a metric: OWA was already tabulated and defined in v6. Revised comparability wording does not specify a concrete replacement setting.

E4.justification: The random-seed sensitivity analysis in Appendix B.3 and Table 16 is removed without replacement. Component, backbone, adapter, and framework-integration ablations remain, as does the Figure 5 case analysis. Its rewritten interpretation does not constitute a new analysis.

E5.justification: v6 explicitly reports seeds 2024, 2025, and 2026, individual-run scores, means, and standard deviations across five datasets and four horizons. v8 removes both Table 16 and the Statistical Stability passage, eliminating the paper's explicit run-to-run uncertainty reporting. This establishes a reporting removal, not that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 9 lower iTransformer's Traffic MSEs by 0.010, changing its average from 0.394 to 0.384 and reversing its ranking against unchanged SE-LLM at 0.386. Table 9 also changes TQNet's ETTh1/96 MSE from 0.379 to 0.370 and iTransformer's ECL/720 MAE from 0.204 to 0.294. Section 4.1 revises the reported relative improvements. TimeMixer++ M4 entries and Table 16 outcomes disappear; retained SE-LLM benchmark scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 revises the attention-complexity expression from O(N^2 K) to O(N^2). Equation 4 changes the mathematical definition of temporal-semantic similarity. Section 3.2 and Algorithm 5 additionally recognize that softmax over a singleton dimension produces all-one weights. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: SE-LLM bridges the modality gap through TSCC and Time-Adapter, improves forecasting, and offers computational efficiency. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: v8 describes AM-VAE as modeling latent semantics rather than directly generating future observations, qualifies Figure 5's anomaly-alignment interpretation, and adds that benefits may be weaker for stable series. It also explains the conditional singleton-softmax degeneracy and removes the statistical-stability interpretation. Appendix D's computational and backbone limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 drops the explicit identification of AutoTimes as the source of adopted AutoTimes, Time-LLM, and iTransformer scores. Section 3.2 removes the statement that AM-VAE omits reconstruction loss, without specifying a replacement objective. Algorithm 5 adds the singleton-softmax qualification. The code link and disclosed top-k and adapter-rank settings remain.

R1.justification: The reference list and substantive positioning against prior forecasting, LLM-alignment, and adapter research remain unchanged. Removing TimeMixer++ from the M4 comparison does not remove its citation or broader positioning.

P1.justification: v8 rewrites selected method explanations, experimental summaries, qualitative interpretations, and the reproducibility statement. It replaces Temporal Pattern Infusion with Structural Prior Infusion and corrects terminology and grammar. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3's connections and labels are revised, and Figure 4's caption is corrected. Tables 2 and 10 lose the TimeMixer++ column, Table 16 is removed, and appendix algorithms and tables shift position. The malformed MASE summation is typeset correctly. The overall visual design and remaining figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v8 improves mathematical consistency, corrects several numerical comparisons, and moderates mechanistic interpretations. However, it removes the only explicit seed-and-dispersion evidence and an M4 comparator, while reducing baseline provenance detail. The PDFs also leave unexplained how the revised TSCC operations relate to the unchanged SE-LLM scores. These clarity gains and losses of empirical support prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
